question: How does poor nutrition affect a patient's recovery after surgery?

options.A: Automatic reduction in daily caloric needs
options.B: Rapid enhancement of immune system function
options.C: Immediate increase in blood pressure levels
options.D: Delayed healing and prolonged hospital stays

explanation: Inadequate nutrition slows down tissue repair, which means the patient stays in the hospital longer. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h1)

question: Why do body cells rely on the food we eat every day?

options.A: Food consumption completely replaces the need for physical rest
options.B: Nutrients provide essential building blocks for metabolism and repair
options.C: Dietary fats eliminate all internal inflammation within hours
options.D: Vitamins store unlimited energy for lifelong cellular survival

explanation: Cells need a steady supply of nutrients from food to build structures and keep body processes running. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h1)

question: Which food group is the main energy source for the brain and nervous system?
explanation: Glucose from carbohydrates is the primary fuel that brain and nerve cells use to function. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h2)

question: A patient healing from a deep pressure sore needs more of which nutrient to rebuild tissue?
explanation: Proteins supply the amino acids required to build new tissue and close wounds. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h2)

question: Eating too much of which substance is strongly linked to high blood pressure?
explanation: Too much sodium causes the body to hold onto water, increasing pressure inside the blood vessels. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h3)

question: How do antioxidants in food help protect the heart and blood vessels?

options.A: By directly dissolving cholesterol plaques inside major arteries
options.B: By stimulating the immediate production of insulin in the pancreas
options.C: By increasing the total volume of circulating red blood cells
options.D: By neutralizing harmful free radicals that damage blood vessels

explanation: Antioxidants calm reactive molecules, lowering stress and preventing damage to the lining of blood vessels. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h3)

question: What happens to the body during severe protein deficiency?
explanation: Without enough dietary protein, the body breaks down its own muscles and struggles to fight off infections. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h4)

question: Why does eating too many calories over a long time lead to metabolic problems?

options.A: Vitamins accumulate in the bloodstream and block oxygen transport
options.B: Saturated fats immediately destroy all endocrine glands in the body
options.C: Excess caloric intake causes insulin resistance and lipid abnormalities
options.D: Overeating causes total failure of the renal filtration system

explanation: Taking in more calories than the body can use leads to fat buildup, blood fat imbalances, and trouble handling insulin. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h4)

question: Which nutrient must pregnant women take early on to help prevent birth defects of the brain and spine?
explanation: Folic acid is vital in early pregnancy for the proper formation of the baby's neural tube. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h5)

question: Why do older adults generally need fewer calories each day than younger adults?

options.A: Their digestive systems completely stop absorbing macronutrients
options.B: Body fat converts into an internal energy source that replaces food
options.C: They experience a decreased basal metabolic rate and lower physical activity
options.D: Older tissue requires zero energy to maintain basic cellular life

explanation: As people age, they naturally lose muscle and move around less, meaning their bodies burn fewer calories. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h5)

question: Which blood test do clinicians check to monitor short-term changes in a patient's protein levels?
explanation: Prealbumin changes quickly in the blood, making it a good marker for recent shifts in nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h6)

question: When a nurse checks a patient's height, weight, and body mass index, what kind of assessment is this?
explanation: Anthropometry simply means measuring the physical dimensions and size of the human body. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h6)

question: Why is it important to respect a patient's cultural background when teaching them about diet?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any follow-up laboratory testing
options.B: It guarantees the patient will never develop a chronic illness later in life
options.C: It is the only legal requirement mandated by hospital administrative policy
options.D: It ensures the meal plan respects traditional eating habits and improves compliance

explanation: Patients are much more likely to follow dietary advice when it fits with the traditional foods they grew up eating. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h7)

question: Which healthcare professional do nurses usually work with to plan special diets for sick patients?
explanation: Registered dietitians are food and nutrition experts who team up with nurses to plan medical nutrition care. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h7)
